title: Repeated whole-cell patch-clamp recording from CA1 pyramidal cells in rodent hippocampal slices followed by axon initial segment labeling
protocol: Anesthetize mouse or rat by placing in an anesthetic chamber containing suitable concentration of isoflurane.
Confirm deep anesthesia, reduction of breathing, and absence of reflexes.
Decapitate rodent using sharp scissors or guillotine.
Rapidly remove skull using fine scissors.
Use curved, blunt-tip forceps to remove the skull from between bregma and the zygomatic arch.
Gently separate brain from skull using a small spatula, taking care to sever cranial nerves.
Transfer brain from small beaker to glass Petri dish lined with filter paper.
Remove cerebellum and frontal third of brain using a scalpel.
Apply a thin film of cyanoacrylate glue to the slicing stage of vibratome.
Place brain, ventral surface down onto the glued slicing stage.
Wash excess glue from brain block using a few drops of sucrose-ACSF applied with a wide-mouth Pasteur pipette.
Flood slicing chamber in vibratome with ice-cold sucrose-ACSF.
Position brain on slicing stage so that entorhinal cortices are closest to the vibratome blade.
Place a carbogen line in the slicing chamber.
Move blade to brain surface.
Cut 400 μm thick horizontal slices containing the hippocampus slowly at a speed of 0.05–0.1 mm/s forward blade movement and with a horizontal blade oscillation of 1–1.5 mm.
Trim the slices and separate them from each hemisphere using a scalpel blade or bent hypodermic needle.
Transfer the trimmed slices to a submerged holding chamber filled with carbogenated sucrose-ACSF pre-warmed to 35°C.
Recover slices in the holding chamber for 30 min.
Transfer the holding chamber to the lab bench at 20°C ± 2°C (room temperature) until the slices are required for recording.
Keep solutions bubbled with 95% O2/5% CO2 at all times.
Transfer hippocampal slice to the recording chamber.
Turn off inflow and outflow of recording ACSF.
Using a wide-mouth Pasteur pipette, transfer a brain slice from the holding chamber to the slice chamber.
Ensure that the dorsal surface is kept upwards during transfer.
Place slice weight over slice, ensuring anchor wires do not overlay the CA1 region of the hippocampus.
Restart recording ACSF flow.
Adjust ACSF flow rate to approximately 4–6 mL/min and ensure it is not recirculated.
Under low magnification (10× objective), identify str. pyramidale of CA1.
Exchange objective lens to high magnification (40× objective).
Identify healthy region of pyramidal cells.
Select ovoid cell bodies that are lightly contrasted with a halo of diffracted light around them.
Avoid shriveled or shrunken cells as they may be damaged or undergoing cell death.
Typically identify a cluster of healthy looking cells located 50–100 μm below the slice surface.
Fill a pre-prepared patch pipette with intracellular solution.
Place the filled patch pipette on the electrode holder.
Coat Ag wire of headstage amplifier with AgCl.
Apply positive pressure to patch pipette via pneumatic tube attached to electrode holder.
Move patch pipette through recording ACSF and park it just above the slice for targeted cell location.
Obtain a whole-cell patch-clamp recording from the first identified CA1 pyramidal cell.
Exclude recordings if resting membrane potential is more depolarized than −50 mV at time of entering whole-cell configuration.
Exclude recordings if access resistance is greater than 30 MΩ or changes by more than 20% during the course of the recording.
Perform intrinsic physiology analysis in current-clamp, including: 30× −10 pA steps from the zero-current level (500 ms duration).
Assess resting membrane potential, input resistance, and membrane time constant.
From a membrane potential of −70 mV, perform 3× families of hyper-to depolarizing current steps (−100 to +400 pA in 25 pA steps, 500 ms duration).
Confirm spontaneous synaptic inputs by recording between 1 and 5 min of continuous recording at −70 mV voltage-clamp.
Close IR-DIC light source and increase exposure time of digital camera (100–200 ms works well).
Move filter turret to correct filter-set for fluorescent dye used.
Form outside-out patch by slowly retracting the patch electrode under visual guidance.
Increase holding potential toward ∼−40 mV when access resistance begins to increase smoothly from 5-30 MΩ to facilitate rupture of the retracted membrane.
Continue retracting pipette until well clear of resealed cell.
Confirm continued presence of filled cell both under IR-DIC and fluorescence.
Repeat procedure for a further 2–4 cells.
Make note of the order of which cells are recorded.
Once all recordings are complete and viability of resealing confirmed, place slice into appropriate treatment.
Stop inflow and outflow of recording ACSF.
Remove slice weight.
Using a wide-mouth Pasteur pipette, remove the slice from the recording chamber and place it in the treatment chamber.
Note the time when slice treatment was started.
Rinse the transfer pipette with distilled water.
Record slices should be treated with different KCl or NaCl in a counterbalanced manner within day and between days.
Optionally base this protocol on the recent study (Booker et al., 2020a) employing prolonged depolarization of neurons by application of 15 mM KCl to examine cell excitability.
Many other methods of modifying cell excitability could be employed, such as 4-aminopyridine, tetraethylammonium, tetrodotoxin, AP-5, CNQX, or bicuculline.
The agent used must be easily and rapidly washed out of the tissue to allow comparison of physiological states under identical conditions.
Repeat the procedure for remaining slices and alternate treatment conditions.
If a break is required after slice treatment, remove the slice from the treatment chamber and return it to the recording chamber.
Ensure that the same side of the slice is positioned up to allow direct access to dye-filled cells.
Place the slice weight on the slice, avoiding the CA1 region of the slice.
Allow 3–5 minutes for ACSF to fully wash out treatment ACSF.
Identify previously filled cells using fluorescence microscopy.
Perform whole-cell patch-clamp recordings on dye-filled cells, starting with the first filled cell and moving through surviving cells.
Re-seal the patch of membrane with outside-out patch formation after recording completion.
Fix slices immediately upon removal from perfusing ACSF, turning off all inflow and outflow pumps.
Remove the slice weight.
Carefully extract the slice using the slice transfer pipette.
Place the slice into a fixation vessel such as a multi-well plate or bijou bottle.
Extract excess recording ACSF using a Pasteur pipette.
Apply 2–3 mL of fresh 4% PFA in PB to the slice.
Swirl or agitate the slice slightly to ensure it is free-floating and not adhered to the wall of the vessel.
Keep slices in 4% PFA at 20°C ± 2°C (room temperature) for 1 h.
Transfer slices into PBS and store at 4°C until used for immunohistochemical labeling.
Wash slices thoroughly in PBS: Remove excess storage PBS from well with plastic Pasteur pipette.
Fill well containing slice with fresh PBS (approx. 3–5 mL).
Repeat washing process 2-3 times to fully remove any residual buffer and PFA.
Allow each wash to last 5-10 minutes per repetition.
Prepare blocking solution containing 10% normal goat serum (NGS), 0.3% Triton X-100, and 0.05% NaN3 in PBS.
Add 0.5 mL of blocking solution to each well of a 24-well plate labeled with unique slice identifiers.
Transfer each brain slice to its corresponding well using a soft, fine paintbrush.
Block slices for 1 hour at 20°C ± 2°C (room temperature) in the blocking solution.
Prepare fresh antibody dilution solution containing 5% NGS, 0.3% Triton X-100, and 0.05% NaN3 diluted in PBS.
Add primary antibodies: Mouse anti-AnkyrinG at 1 μg/mL or 1:1,000 of neat antisera and Rabbit anti-NeuN at 1 μg/mL or 1:1,000 of neat antisera to the antibody dilution solution.
Incubate slices with primary antibodies for 1 hour at room temperature.
Transfer slices to their respective well with a paintbrush.
Rinse the brush in clean PBS between each slice transfer.
Cover the 24-well plate with Parafilm to prevent buffer evaporation.
Place the 24-well plate on an orbital shaker in a cool room or fridge.
Incubate slices for at least 18 to 24 hours (overnight) at 4°C.
Fill clean multi-well plates with PBS buffer.
Transfer each slice from the primary antibody plate to the PBS buffer using a fine paintbrush.
Remove excess storage PBS from the well using a plastic Pasteur pipette.
Fill the well containing the slice with fresh PBS (approximately 3–5 mL).
Repeat washing in PBS two to three more times to fully remove residual buffer.
Each wash should last for 5 to 10 minutes.
Prepare secondary antibody buffer: 3% NGS, 0.3% Triton X-100, and 0.05% NaN3 in PBS.
Add Goat anti-Mouse Alexa Fluor 488 at 4 μg/mL or 1:500 neat sera to the buffer.
Add Goat anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 633 at 4 μg/mL or 1:500 neat sera to the buffer.
Reconstitute streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 568 conjugate at 4 μg/mL or 1:500 of neat sera.
Add 0.5 mL of prepared antibody solution to each well of a fresh, clean 24-well plate.
Transfer slices to their corresponding wells with a paintbrush, rinsing the brush in clean PBS between slices.
Cover the 24-well plate with lab film (i.e., Parafilm) to prevent evaporation of buffer.
Place the 24-well plate on an orbital shaker in a cool room or fridge.
Incubate for 18 to 24 hours at 4°C.
Fill clean multi-well plates with PBS buffer.
Transfer slice from primary antibody plate to PBS buffer using a fine paintbrush.
Remove excess storage PBS from well with plastic Pasteur pipette.
Fill well containing slice with fresh PBS (approx. 3–5 mL).
Repeat the wash process for 2–3 times to fully remove any residual buffer.
Washes should last 5–10 minutes per repetition.
Fill clean multi-well plates with 0.1 M PB buffer (3–5 mL/well).
Transfer slice from PBS buffer to PB buffer using a fine paintbrush.
Rinse paintbrush between transfers.
Stir on orbital shaker for 10–15 min.
Remove excess storage PB from well with plastic Pasteur pipette.
Fill well containing slice with fresh PB (approx. 3–5 mL).
Stir on orbital shaker for 1 h.
Label glass microscope slide with unique slice identifier and antibodies used.
Remove slice from PB multi-well plate using paintbrush.
Blot excess PB from slice by touching brush to a piece of tissue.
Gently lay slice on slide.
Place sufficient fluorescent mounting medium (e.g., Vectashield Hardset mounting medium) on slice (2–3 drops for 22 × 22 mm coverslip).
Lay coverslip over slice from one edge, then slowly allow remainder of coverslip to fall into place.
Place mounted slides in a cool, dark place for 1–2 h to allow hardset mounting medium to harden.
Seal coverslips with nail polish around the edge.
Place slides in slide box for at least 1 day before imaging.
Keep slides at 4°C for a few days if necessary before imaging.
Ensure images are taken within the first 2 weeks post-immunohistochemistry to avoid deterioration of labeling quality.
Place slices at 20°C ± 2°C ∼15 min prior to imaging to allow warming to ambient temperature.
Identify the CA1 region by the presence of streptavidin labeling of filled neurons under epifluorescent imaging and a low magnification objective (×10 or ×20).
Set appropriate light path for confocal imaging according to the fluorophores used.
Exchange objective lens to a 63× oil immersion objective after applying a small amount of immersion medium.
Acquire high-resolution Z-stacks through CA1 using volume imaging function of the confocal microscope (1,024 × 1,024 xy resolution, pixel size: 0.14 μm, 1 μm z steps).
Place histological slide in microscope.
Under low magnification (i.e., 10× or 20× Objective lens) identify the CA1 region of the slice.
Apply a small amount (1–2 drops) of immersion medium and exchange objective lens.
Use the appropriate immersion medium for your objective lens, according to manufacturer’s guidelines.
Under high magnification identify the str. pyramidale layer of CA1.
Set the top and bottom extents of your 3-dimensional volume using the volume imaging function of your confocal microscope.
Set the z-step size to 0.13 μm.
Establish optimal laser power and detector gain settings for start and end of volume.
If microscope is capable, set values to automatically modulate over the slice depth.
Acquire image stack at 2,048 × 2,048 resolution under 2× zoom, which gives a pixel width of 0.04 μm.
